profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record in Hillsboro, Oregon carries the name Verizon Hillsboro Tanasbourne Data Center with operator tagged as Verizon Business. Hillsboro is a well-established data center market in the Portland metro area, and third-party colocation directories list roughly forty five distinct operators active there, none of which this research identified as Verizon-operated commercial space, which is a signal against this being an active colocation facility open to outside tenants. Verizon prior data center footprint traces mainly to its 2011 acquisition of Terremark, a colocation and cloud provider, but Verizon divested that Terremark-descended commercial data center business twice: first selling a set of European and Latin American data centers to Equinix in a roughly 3.5 billion dollar deal announced in late 2016 and closed in 2017 covering 29 data centers across 15 markets, and separately selling its remaining Terremark-branded US cloud and colocation operations to IBM around May 2017. Equinix current published footprint does not include an Oregon market, and the Equinix 2017 acquisition list does not appear to have included any Pacific Northwest facility, so this Hillsboro building does not match the known Equinix-acquired set. It is possible this record reflects a legacy or since-repurposed Verizon or Terremark-era facility, stale OSM tagging carried over from an earlier company presence, or genuine but undocumented current Verizon Business network infrastructure. Oregon sits outside Verizon nine-state incumbent local exchange carrier territory, which weighs against a legacy regional Bell explanation. No operator fact sheet, county assessor record, or trade-press source confirming an active Verizon-operated facility at this address was found this session. Given the ambiguity, this record is presented as an honest open question rather than a confirmed operating data center, and no capacity, square footage, tier, or year-built figures are asserted.

reading.body:
This facility is referenced only in a tier-4 aggregator and not in any Verizon operator publication this research has accessed. Verizon Business divested 29 data centers to Equinix in 2017, and the current operator status of this Hillsboro location is uncertain. Research budget is exhausted and this facility carries no published power specification.

Oregon has 133 mapped data center facilities, of which 8 have published power figures totaling 156.6 megawatts. This campus does not appear in that set, which means it either publishes no capacity figure or the figure is not yet in this site's database.

Without published specifications, this facility cannot be ranked among Oregon's active AI infrastructure or assessed for relevance to grid constraints on compute scaling.
